newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour would keep EU veto in key areas.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour would keep EU veto in key areas.

text.p: The opposition Labour party's foreign affairs spokesman, Robin Cook, said on Tuesday a Labour government would keep Britain's veto in the European Union over any changes in taxation or border controls.
But he said additional qualified majority voting in some areas of social policy might be necessary to streamline Europe and reform policies like the Common Agricultural Policy.
"We will keep the veto.. for strategic areas like taxation, external border controls and foreign and security policy," Cook told a BBC radio interviewer.
But he added: "If you want reform, frankly in many cases you do have to have majority voting to stop one, perhaps small, nation obstructing progress.

"We want to see reform in, for instance, the structural funds, we want to see reform across areas of agricultural policy, and that will mean there'll have to be majority votes taken against those individual nations that stand in the way."

Cook's comments echo Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown, who said earlier in the day that Labour would not allow majority voting on immigration, foreign affairs, border controls or taxation. "The British veto will remain on all these issues."
